 It only took weeks after Matt Rhule's hiring before the first of eventually many social media warriors took to the interwebs to call for his firing. Assistant coaches have also been the targets of digitized stones, usually the coordinators. Some of the calls are deserved, some not.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement When Dana Holgorsen was hired, he seemed to be the answer to Nebraska's prayers. Prior to his years as a head coach, he was a master offensive technician as his teams at Texas Tech, Houston and Oklahoma State were always in the top 10 nationally in both points and total yards. Alas, it never took off at Nebraska and his name began being touted for dismissal online as this year's 4-game losing streak progressed and the point totals notched in those losses were only 17, 17, 10 and 13 plus many penalty yards amassed.
 Matt Rhule was thinking along the same lines and finally pulled the trigger a week ago Saturday.
 The question asked of you was the timing – too soon, too late or just right?
 The majority felt the time had come – 53% 
 Of the remaining choices, too late at 32% more than doubled the too quick crowd at 15% 
 Guess it's time to start thinking about next season's permanent replacement? 
 I'm sort of against it, but I would probably vote for it, since the committee would likely use it more for a blueblood's cash and traveling fan base than merit. Yeah, call me jaded. 
 I don't blame the Maryland fans, here – I did not see that upset coming 
 I love the the fact Michigan fans think Whittingham was actually the problem, and not everything that's been going on at Michigan since 2021. It might be best to stick with him. Or else, maybe he had no idea how deep things run there & would be thrilled to take his buyout and retire peacefully if offered.
